entities.text: Shivappa Vadari vs The Divisional Manager
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Indi, Vijayapur (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.1618/2015 vide its judgment and award dated 03.01.2020.

2. The claimant is the daughter of the deceased - Shilavanthi, who died in a road traffic accident on 13.06.2015 while travelling in a bus belonging to the respondent - Corporation bearing registration No.KA-17/F-1522.

The claimant claimed that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.5,000/- per month and that she was contributing the same to the claimant and that due to her death, the claimant was deprived of the emotional and financial support.
Hence, she filed a claim petition claiming compensation from the Corporation.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the Corporation who denied the accident as well as the death of the mother of the claimant.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5516 and she marked Exs.P1 to 3.
The Corporation did not lead any evidence.
5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation.
It held that the deceased was 40 years at the time of the accident and the claimant was married and therefore, she was not dependent on the deceased.
The Tribunal therefore, awarded a sum of Rs.75,000/-.
The Tribunal directed the Corporation to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed by the claimant.

7. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that though the deceased was a married daughter,
she was entitled to claim compensation as the deceased was with her and she was dependent on the deceased.

He contended that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company NC: 2023:KHC-K:5516 Limited vs. Birender and others [(2020) 11 SCC 356] had held that even married daughters are entitled to claim as dependants.

entities.text: National Insurance Company NC: 2023:KHC-K:5516 Limited vs. Birender and others [(2020) 11 SCC 356]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He therefore, contended that compensation to which the claimant is entitled to, deserves to be re-determined by considering the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month and factoring 25% towards loss of future prospects.

2 8.

entities.text: Shivappa Vadari vs The Divisional Manager on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the Corporation contended that the claimant herself claimed that the deceased was earning Rs.5,000/- per month and therefore, the question of considering her income at a sum of Rs.8,000/- does not arise.
He however, did not dispute that the deceased was 40 years old and therefore, the claimant was entitled to loss of future prospects at 25%.
9. In view of the above, the claimant is undoubtedly entitled to claim compensation for the death of her mother in a road traffic accident.
The issue is squarely covered by the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Birender and others, supra.
In that view of the matter, the impugned judgment and award refusing to grant compensation on the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5516 ground that the claimant was married daughter deserves to be set aside.

Hence, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation by considering the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and factoring the loss of future prospects at 25% of the income.

10. Consequently, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation, which is re-determined as follows:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Towards loss of dependency 6,75,000/-
 (6,000 + 25% x 12 x 15 x )
 2 Towards loss of parental 40,000/-
 consortium  3 Towards loss of estate, funeral 30,000/-
 expenses etc.,
 Total 7,45,000/-
 11.

Since the liability of the Corporation is not challenged, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
12. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.75,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.7,45,000/-, which is payable by the Corporation along with interest at the rate of NC: 2023:KHC-K:5516 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

13. The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the Corporation before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
14. Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
